rule:
Every catalyst rate law in backend/amcrax/data/kinetics.yaml and every catalyst named by the author is given exactly
one class at the AmCraX conditions (20 bar; study temperatures 450-700 degC; operating points 499-594 degC):

amcrax_conditions.note: standalone and integrated studies at 20 bar (pressure studies 1.013-40 bar); operating points = lowest T for 95 % conversion with 100 kg catalyst per 100 kmol/h NH3 (results/research/aspen_kinetic/catalyst_comparison.json)

statement: No AmCraX kinetic law is validated at 20 bar. Every kinetic result at 20 bar is a pressure extrapolation; Takahashi laws are additionally unvalidated at 1 atm (failed figure predictions).

laws.reason: lucentini2019ceo2 gives conversion curves and TOFs only (63 % at 450 degC, 1 atm, GHSV 3067 h-1, Ar:NH3 1.3:1); no rate equation, Ea, orders or pre-exponential factor. Phase 2 search found no complete published law for Ni/CeO2.

laws.reason: main text read in full on 24 Nov 2026 (research/notes/sayas2020_full_text.md); it gives the rate-law form (power law with an approach-to-equilibrium term, eqns (1)-(2)), the orders 0.5 (NH3) and -1.2 (H2) and an apparent Ea of 75 kJ/mol at 350 degC and 1 atm (Table 4), but NO complete rate law: the rate constant (pre-exponential factor, units) and the equilibrium term of the integral fit are in the supplementary information, which was not obtained. Nothing was fitted or estimated. The 10-40 bar conversions are stored as literature comparison points that no model uses.
laws.reason_superseded_2026_11_23: full text and SI not obtainable by automated access (HTTP 403 / connection closed, 23 Nov 2026, Phase 1 and Phase 2); the abstract gives conditions (1-40 bar, 250-550 degC, WHSV 9000-30000 mL g-1 h-1) but no pre-exponential factor; no parameter is estimated.

experimental.conversion_note: about 84 % at 550 degC and 40 bar (figure reading; the text says 'around 80 %'); 15 points at 10-40 bar, 350-550 degC

Nothing was fitted or estimated. The 10-40 bar conversions are stored as literature comparison points that no model uses.

literature_comparison_points_sayas2020.description: The 15 measured conversions of 3%Ru10%K/CaO at 10, 20 and 40 bar (Fig. 4A, figure readings). Literature comparison points only: NOT used by any model, fit or rule (addendum of 24 November 2026).
literature_comparison_points_sayas2020.catalyst: 3%Ru10%K/CaO (ICP 2.8 wt% Ru, 9.6 wt% K), 200 mg, 300-500 um, diluted in 1 g SiC
literature_comparison_points_sayas2020.conditions: pure NH3, 30 N mL/min (WHSV 9000 mL gcat-1 h-1) at every pressure, isothermal set-point, fresh catalyst, 7 h

uncertainty.flow_reference_state: 'N mL' not defined: 0 or 25 degC, about 9 % in F
uncertainty.bed: reactor diameter, bed length and temperature profile not given

cross_catalyst_context_sayas2020.description: Context only, NOT a test of any law: the existing AmCraX Ru/Al2O3 law (Kum et al. 2026, fitted at 1-10 bar on an 8 wt% Ru commercial catalyst) evaluated at the Sayas test conditions with the SAME ruthenium per mol of NH3 fed. The two catalysts differ (support, promoter, dispersion), so a difference says nothing about either law's validity.
cross_catalyst_context_sayas2020.label: cross-catalyst context comparison, not a test of the law
cross_catalyst_context_sayas2020.law: ru_kum_temkin_pyzhev (kinetics.yaml), isothermal PFR, keq_basis amcrax_thermo, pure NH3, no pressure drop
cross_catalyst_context_sayas2020.law_fitted_range: 1-10 bar, 350-450 degC (Kum et al. fit to Di Carlo et al. 2014)
cross_catalyst_context_sayas2020.reading: at equal Ru per mol NH3 the pressure-extrapolated Ru/Al2O3 law converts far more than the measured Ru-K/CaO at 20 bar and 500 degC; this is a reason to keep the Ru/Al2O3 20 bar results labelled as extrapolation, which the project already does, not evidence under the verdict rules
